requirements.desc: For a managed-worktree acceptance-decision, the lifecycle operation shall retain the selected binding's runId, Issue, and spec identity through its flow-state write and shall mutate only that bound flow.json.
requirements.note: R1: acceptance-decision persists only the exact bound worktree flow identity

requirements.desc: The acceptance-decision success path shall not call an active-flow registry remove, park, or document-replacement operation, and it shall verify that the target entry and every entry present before the operation remain registered with their original modes.
requirements.note: R2: success preserves registry document identity and cannot remove, park, or replace it

requirements.desc: After a successful managed-worktree acceptance-decision, guarded flow resolution shall return the same runId, Issue, and spec and the flow state shall mark acceptance-decision done and final-regression in progress only for accept_risk_and_continue.
requirements.note: R3: guarded resolution retains identity and only continue advances final regression

requirements.desc: A worktree binding mismatch, registry operation lock failure, registry revision conflict, or registry identity verification failure shall return an explicit failure without reporting a successful acceptance-decision transition and without losing any pre-operation registry entry.
requirements.note: R4: every binding and registry failure leaves flow state and pointers unchanged

requirements.desc: Regression coverage shall prove registry preservation and guarded target resolution with at least two managed-worktree flows, inject each R4 failure boundary without entry loss, prove that a one-entry registry retains its entry after accept_risk_and_continue, and prove that flow resume --parked restores a parked target's active entry and exact target resolution.
requirements.note: R5: two-flow, single-flow, and parked-resume regressions preserve exact pointers

requirements.desc: For one current flow and one mechanically blocked gate attempt, missing materialized repair evidence may invoke the existing impl-repair authority at most once, invalidate only leaf steps from test-execute through finalize-cleanup, and permit one subsequent test-review-gate evaluation; a further failure shall not invoke the recovery again. For one exhausted rejected review record with a changed tree, the existing review-convergence authority shall clear only that record's stale fields and permit exactly one semantic re-evaluation without mutating unrelated flow state.
requirements.note: R6: bounded repair and semantic review recovery invalidate only stale current-flow evidence

entries.reason: Draft coverage review PASS artifact was written, but its post-hook reported a repository operation lock failure.
entries.resolution: Preserved the generated review artifact and followed the guarded next-action state after the post-hook warning.

entries.reason: The requirement says to fix the lifecycle so one flow update does not lose registry entries, but leaves the exact lifecycle boundary and implementation behavior to later investigation, so two reviewers could disagree on what implementati...
Draft gate found the lifecycle boundary and failure criteria too deferred for reproducible implementation review.
entries.resolution: Will replace deferred investigation language with verified module ownership and explicit success and failure behavior.

entries.reason: Scenario validity was blocked before tests ran because git diff against base branch reports pre-existing implementation-target paths; the spec-local test process did not start.
entries.resolution: Inspect branch/base divergence and resolve the flow preflight baseline without altering unrelated source changes.

entries.reason: Rebasing the worktree branch onto main was blocked because flow artifacts and the new spec-local test are intentionally uncommitted; no rebase was applied.
entries.resolution: Use the worktree-local autostash rebase path so the active-flow artifacts are restored automatically.

entries.reason: Static test review reached a tooling error while recording duplicate findingId values; a contemporaneous issue-log write transiently returned NO_FLOW, while guarded status immediately afterward resolved the intended flow.
entries.resolution: Inspect the generated review findings for duplicated identifiers, preserve the transient registry evidence, and repair tooling before the one permitted retry.

entries.reason: Test review rejected R4 because lock/revision faults were injected through a manager facade and failure persistence did not assert the absence of a successful decision record.
entries.resolution: Inject errors at ActiveFlowRegistry.load and snapshot decision artifact plus issue log to prove no successful transition is reported.

entries.reason: Add a locked active-flow snapshot with a revision receipt so acceptance-decision can fail closed on lock and revision failures.
Bind rollback to the same captured FlowTargetExpectation so verification failures cannot restore the original state into a different flow.
Reused the captured exact-target mutation closure for rollback, which now fails closed if the original target no longer resolves.
entries.resolution: Rollback is bound to the same runId, Issue, and spec as the forward mutation.

entries.reason: fix: match the acceptance target against the full registry identity key
entries.resolution: Target presence now compares runId, Issue, spec, and mode together, matching the preserved entry-set invariant.

entries.reason: fix: exclude canonical impl review evidence from stale fingerprint refresh
entries.resolution: Canonical typed review evidence already validates the phase artifact, so its older fingerprint must not trigger a test evidence refresh.

entries.reason: The diff adds a non-trivial baseline worktree execution layer for scenario-validity, but the provided spec and acknowledgment evidence do not confirm this architecture or data-flow direction.
fix: remove unrelated scenario-validity baseline worktree execution
entries.resolution: The baseline worktree path was outside the active specification and triggered the no-overengineering guardrail, so the scenario-validity preflight remains unchanged.
